title: adaptive-provisioning-pacer-for-steady-degradation-and-burst-smoothing
author: Maya Chen
description: Introduce an adaptive provisioning pacer that smooths autoscaler decisions across dedicated fleets by applying a gamma-weighted pacing window to reservation and burst allocations. Motivation: recent incidents showed repeated oscillation when tens of tenants simultaneously ramp causing flapping autoscaler decisions and transient SLA slippage. This PR implements a pacing layer between the decision engine and provisioner so that scale up/down intents are rate-limited with stateful momentum, tenant-level dampening, and configurable burst forgiveness. The change touches three areas: 1) decision smoothing: a new Pacer module that consumes scale intents and emits paced deltas using a configurable half-life and gamma decay parameter; 2) budget and burst integration: pacer respects per-tenant guaranteed throughput envelopes and optional ephemeral burst credits; it can defer non-critical adjustments to preserve headroom; 3) instrumentation and alerting: adds metrics for pacer_active, pacer_output_delta, pacer_rejections, and tenant_pacer_latency plus dashboards and an alert when pacing causes more than 3 consecutive deferred scale operations. Includes unit tests for edge-cases, an integration test that replays historical incident traces, and a canary job for dedicated clusters. Backwards compatible: pacer is off by default and enabled through the autoscaler.policy.pacer config. See linked Linear items for rollout plan and experiment gating.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can we avoid tenant starvation when multiple pacer defers pile up? Please add a fairness check.
Maya Chen: Added a fairness window and unit tests for starvation scenarios (see pacer_test.go). Also clarified behavior in docs.
Priya Singh: Integration test showed a small memory spike in the canary job — can we cap in-memory intent queue and persist overflow to the redis-backed queue?
Maya Chen: Implemented bounded queue with persistent spillover; reran canary and memory stayed stable.
Rafael Torres: Metrics look good but add an SLI that ties pacer-induced deferrals to SLO degradation so we can auto-disable if needed.
Maya Chen: Added tenant_pacer_deferral_ratio SLI and an emergency disable flag controlled via autoscaler.policy.pacer.enabled=false.
release_notes: Adaptive provisioning pacer: opt-in pacing layer to smooth dedicated cluster autoscaler actions, reduce oscillation, and integrate tenant burst budgets. Config via autoscaler.policy.pacer (half_life, gamma, max_queue_size, enable_spillover). Observability: new pacer metrics and dashboards. Rollout: canary in dedicated clusters followed by gradual enablement per-tenant.
notes_on_rollout: Canary deployed to two dedicated clusters in us-west-2 for 72h. Feature gate off by default. Rollout plan in ENG-3421: enable for low-risk tenants (10%) for 24h then ramp based on pacer_deferral_ratio SLI.
post_merge_actions: Create runtime-gate in Console to toggle pacer per-tenant; add regression alert to SRE runbook; schedule 1-week telemetry review in ENG-3499.
incident_tie_in: This work is a direct mitigation for SUP-1182 where a spike in background batch workloads caused repeated scale flaps and SLA degradation for interactive tenants. The pacer prevents rapid oscillation by enforcing momentum and honoring guaranteed envelopes.
additional_context: The gamma decay algorithm uses a configurable decay coefficient to weight recent intents more heavily while still preserving a tail for older requests. This choice gives predictable smoothing for bursty traffic patterns compared to simple exponential smoothing used previously. Benchmarks in perf/bench/pacer show 12-18% reduction in scale operations and a 35% decrease in transient SLA errors under synthetic multi-tenant replay workloads.
